turns.user: how do I do a deadlift
turns.reply:
To do a conventional deadlift, here is the setup: stand with feet hip-width apart, bar over mid-foot, grip just outside your legs, and drop your hips until your shins touch the bar. 

Pull your chest up to flatten your back, brace your stomach, and push the floor away. Drive your hips forward at the top, then hinge at the hips to lower it back down.

Keeping the bar glued to your legs protects your lower back and puts the work right on your glutes and hamstrings! 💪

turns.reply:
Here is the complete deadlift breakdown, from setup to lock-out:

1. Stand with feet hip-width apart, bar over mid-foot, roughly an inch from your shins.
2. Hinge down and grip the bar just outside your legs, keeping arms straight.
3. Bend your knees until your shins touch the bar, keeping the bar over mid-foot.
4. Pull your chest up to flatten your lower back, and pull the slack out of the bar.
5. Take a deep breath into your stomach and brace hard.
6. Push the floor away through your heels to break the bar off the ground.
7. Keep the bar dragging up your shins and thighs in a straight line.
8. Drive your hips forward to lock out, standing tall without leaning back.
9. Hinge your hips back to lower the bar past your knees before bending them to touch down.
